summary: The code is syntactically correct and runs, with robust data loading and a plausible ABM loop covering social influence, information diffusion, and a Day-10 policy. However, it misses key required functionality: no calibration to observed data, no computation of required evaluation metrics (e.g., RMSE to observed), no validation criteria checks, and no per-agent predictions for days 30–39. Supply constraints are not enforced because mask inventory is never consumed. Some logic and minor import/performance issues also exist. The required direct main() call is present.

issues.description: No calibration procedure (e.g., grid_search) is implemented, and the model does not optimize parameters to minimize RMSE_to_observed as specified.
issues.solution: Implement a calibration loop (e.g., grid search over specified parameter bounds) that runs the simulation over the training window (days 0–29), aggregates simulated adoption rates, computes RMSE_to_observed against empirical aggregates from train_data.csv, and selects the best parameters.

issues.description: Required evaluation metrics (RMSE_to_observed, MAE_to_observed, R2_to_observed, enforcement_cost, inventory_outage_days) are not computed.
issues.solution: Aggregate observed adoption from train_data.csv, compute RMSE/MAE/R2 against simulated adoption for the calibration window. Track enforcement_cost during the run and inventory_outage_days from the retailer stock state. Output these in results.

issues.description: Does not produce per-agent predictions for mask-wearing during days 30–39 as required; only aggregate time series is stored.
issues.solution: Store and output per-agent is_mask_wearing states for days 30–39 (e.g., a DataFrame with columns day, agent_id, is_mask_wearing).

issues.description: Supply constraint is ineffective: mask inventory is never consumed when agents wear masks, so inventory does not limit adoption.
issues.location: Simulation.run (commented out consumption) and RetailMarket interaction
issues.solution: Deduct one unit of mask_inventory when an agent transitions from not wearing to wearing (0->1) each day, or deduct per day while wearing, with safeguards to avoid negative inventory.

issues.description: Validation criteria (calibration_rmse_threshold, convergence_stability, bounds_respect, directional_validity) are not checked.
issues.solution: After calibration, verify RMSE <= threshold; implement convergence checks; enforce parameter bounds during calibration; run sensitivity tests (e.g., increase mandate effect or enforcement) and assert adoption does not decrease.

issues.description: Entity classes (Person, Household, Location, GovernmentAgency, MediaChannel, Retailer) have placeholder behaviors and are not integrated into the simulation logic.
issues.solution: Either remove unused stubs to reduce confusion or implement their behaviors and integrate with the simulation loop, aligning with the specified attributes and interactions.

issues.description: Metrics.threshold_crossing_time ignores start_day for iteration and returns t - start_day even if t < start_day, which can yield negative times.
issues.solution: Iterate from start_day (for t in range(start_day, len(y))) and return the absolute day index or the elapsed days since start_day consistently.

issues.description: Observation noise is added to adoption_rate_daily, which should represent the simulated value; this may corrupt metric calculations if used.
issues.solution: Keep adoption_rate_daily as the true simulated metric without noise; add a separate observed/adversarially noised series only if needed for synthetic observation modeling.

issues.description: Mismatch with task parameters: several specified parameters (e.g., base_adoption_rate, adherence_decay_rate from spec) are not present or used; parameter bounds and enforcement penalty are not respected/enforced.
issues.solution: Align parameter names and usage with the task specification, enforce bounds during calibration, and integrate adherence decay/compliance fatigue as specified.

issues.description: matplotlib.pyplot is imported but not used.
issues.solution: Remove unused import or add optional plotting guarded by availability.
